verdicts.note: Essay on trends in family sociology; conjugal versus extended forms appear as a typology, not an exposure.

Family structure against fertility in Hong Kong, explicitly modelling the mediation through age at marriage and insisting on temporal correspondence between exposure and outcome. That temporal-correspondence framing is the anticipation threat handled directly.
Marine-product consumption by household pattern.
Immunisation compliance in toddlers; children living at home is a covariate.
Sociodemographic determinants of leaving the parental household in six Latin American countries, World Fertility Survey. Exposure-trend baseline, no fertility outcome.
Family life cycle stages and social change; descriptive typology.
Family structure of origin against the timing of home-leaving, Canadian Family History Survey. Link 1 with a driver, no births.
Disability and attainment of adult status; independent household formation is an outcome of impairment, not of the arrangement.
Postpartum abstinence and birth spacing in tropical Africa. A.14's.
Canadian life-course and kin-availability review; the empty nest is one stage described.
Family-status life table for China with three-generation co-residence as a state; formal, no effect estimate.
Married women's labour force participation in Korea; household composition is collected but the outcome is employment.
Age profile of complex-household residence in Sri Lanka; establishes the stem-family exposure pattern, no fertility outcome.

No abstract. The title -- childrearing versus childbearing, co-residence of mother and child in sub-Saharan Africa -- names co-residence but of mother and CHILD, which is a different construct; not decidable from the title.
Predictors of depression in middle-aged women.
Courgeau's survey linking migration, leaving home, marriage and childbearing as interacting life events. The joint-determination problem of §3, studied as such; worth a full-text read.
Model schedule for leaving the parental home AFTER MARRIAGE in China -- the extended-couple to nuclear transition. Exposure trend, no fertility estimate.
Plasmid conjugal transfer genes. 'Coresident plasmid' and 'fertility' are the bacterial senses -- a clean homonym pair on both axes at once.
No abstract; modernisation and household formation on St Bart, title not decisive on outcome.
Family planning services for people with mental disorder.

Industrialisation against farm household complexity in 274 Taiwanese townships, finding extension INCREASES with industrialisation. A driver-to-arrangement result that contradicts the modernisation prior; no fertility outcome.
Congress report; nuptiality and household formation are session titles.
Determinants of leaving the parental home, Netherlands Fertility Survey 1988. Link 1.
Review of determinants of marriage postponement in Japan. A.7's.
Caregiving burden of middle-aged children supporting parents who live independently. The homonym, and not even co-resident.
Family risk factors and the timing of 'emancipation' among heroin users -- the emancipation homonym in the wild, and a reminder of why that term was kept out of the cause axis.
No abstract; 'The family histories of Australian women' is not decisive.
Psychology of change and transition; an edited collection on life transitions generally.
Regional demography methods volume.
China's fertility transition and the one-child policy; elderly care appears as a consequence, not an exposure.
Demographic equilibrium in late-medieval Essex; pre-modern, and the arrangement is not the exposure.
Regional profile of Amazonia; household formation is one statistic listed.
Letter on pregnancy during surgical residency.
Transitions in young adulthood in Great Britain, including leaving the family of origin and establishing one's own. Sequence description.
Population ageing driven by the falling birth rate, and its consequences for household formation and housing. The arrow runs from fertility to households.

Parental co-residence at marriage in Japan, 9,000 couples from the Ninth National Fertility Survey, with birth order and intergenerational transfers. Link 1's second half in the setting the extended arm needs.
Qualitative study of 80 young Britons who left home before 21, covering courtship, family formation and single parenthood. No estimate but directly on the pre-launch mechanism.
Coping in families with a member with intellectual disability living at home.
No abstract; stepfamily versus nuclear coping during pregnancy is decisive on subject.
Family life cycle stages in China, computed from fertility rates.

Parental divorce against leaving home, cohabitation, marriage AND birth in one Dutch analysis. The exposure is parental divorce rather than the arrangement, but it estimates both links in the same data, which is the boundary-spanning design the chapter is short of. Full-text read.
Relational model of post-nuptial home-leaving in China, on Brass-Gompertz lines. Method, not estimate.
Programmatic essay on household demography's research strategy.

METADATA MISMATCH: the title is 'Mate Selection and Fertility in Urban Nigeria' but the indexed abstract is the Korean working-class couples study on marital adjustment by co-residence. One of the two records is mis-attached; cannot be screened until the record is resolved.
Essay on the methods of historical demography.

Log-logistic hazard analysis of first, second and third birth timing in Japan since the 1960s, reporting that CO-RESIDING WITH THE COUPLE'S PARENTS RAISES all three birth hazards irrespective of the wife's employment. A direct extended-arm estimate with the predicted positive sign, and it separates the labour-supply channel.
Review essay on Durkheim, Le Play and family change.
Childhood family of origin against adult male earnings.
Commentary on the Japanese parental-coresidence-and-marriage analyses, tying late marriage to very low fertility. Framing for the extended arm's setting.
Attitudes to marital and intergenerational relationships, Japanese opinion survey. D.2.b's.
Rwandan legal marriage age decree.
Critique of The Truly Disadvantaged; household formation is one of four linking domains discussed.

No indexed abstract, but the title is decisive in the positive direction: household STRUCTURE as the exposure against women's economic activity AND fertility, recent mothers in urban Mexico. One of the two records the boolean query could not reach and that were hand-added on 226.
Prevalence of one-person households across regions; descriptive note.
Prevalence of polygyny and patrilocality in Shipibo villages as an index of cultural change; residence pattern is the outcome, not fertility.
